subject: App integration kickoff: SDK setup, endpoint migration & rate-limit guidance

Diego / Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to start the integration work and want to align on a plan for SDK setup, endpoint migration (we currently call a hosted inference endpoint), and operational guardrails (retries, timeouts, rate limits). A few specific asks up front:

- Do you have recommended SDK config snippets for Node and Python we can drop into our services?
- If we move from your v1 inference endpoints to the v2 runtime you mentioned, what’s the recommended migration path to avoid downtime?
- How do you suggest handling 429s / throttling? Any client-side retry/backoff patterns you prefer?
- We're also going to run this behind our API gateway with a 5s per-request timeout; need guidance if that's sufficient.

Sharing the SOO and initial SOW (attached). Can we get a 30–45 minute kickoff next week? Available windows: Tue/Wed AM PT.

Thanks,

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Integration kickoff: Foliage Health + Redwood Inference

Chris — thanks for this and for the SOW. Happy to lead the technical handoff. Quick draft plan below; we can walk through it in the kickoff.

1) Kickoff (30-45m): Introductions, success criteria, timelines, and owners.
2) Sandbox integration (2 weeks): Ship SDK snippets + small sample app; validate auth, basic calls, streaming behavior.
3) Endpoint migration runbook: smoke tests, staged rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%), monitoring hooks; rollback playbook.
4) Production cutover: schedule short maintenance window if you want to pin traffic, otherwise use traffic-splitting for zero-downtime.

High-level answers to your bullets:
- SDKs: we maintain official Node and Python SDKs. We'll attach a short config doc and paste small snippets in the kickoff. The defaults are safe but we recommend an explicit retry/backoff and a token-scarcity-aware batching policy for heavy throughput paths.
- Migration: avoid a single big cut; route a % of traffic to v2 for 24–48h and monitor latency/error/TOK consumption. Use our rollout API to shift weights.
- 429 handling: client-side exponential backoff with capped jitter + respecting Retry-After header. If you have an API gateway, prefer to propagate 429s for service-level throttling and implement a token bucket on the gateway for preemptive shaping.
- Timeouts: 5s is OK for typical short prompts, but for longer context windows or streaming responses you'll want a higher per-request timeout (15–30s) or switch to streaming so you don't tie up gateway slots.

I'll attach the config doc and a suggested mutual action plan before the kickoff. Monica will own onboarding milestones and the checklist. Proposed kickoff: Tue 2026-02-24 09:30 PT — does that work?

Cheers,
Diego
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Integration kickoff: Integration checklist & next steps

Hi Chris — looping in Rishi and Marissa for commercial/TS touches. Diego and I will drive onboarding. Attaching the checklist CSV for the integration milestones.

Action items I propose before kickoff:
- Foliage: Share a short inventory of services that will call Redwood (names/endpoints).
- Redwood: Provide Node/Python snippets + a short runbook for endpoint migration.
- Security: Fill out SOC2 questionnaire (we can discuss exemptions at kickoff).

Config recommendations (summary):
- Timeouts: set client-side per-request to 15s for sync calls; for streaming set server-side read windows and allow 60s+ for long streams.
- Retries: up to 4 attempts max; exponential backoff starting at 200ms, multiplier 2, with full jitter; respect Retry-After if present.
- Rate limits: implement a token-bucket limiter at the caller plus a fallback queue with TTL 30s, and bubble 429s to calling services for visibility.
- Idempotency: use request_id headers for user-level operations where retries could cause duplication.

We'll also include sample interceptors for common frameworks (Express/Koa and FastAPI) in the SDK samples so it's drop-in.

Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

- Migration: we'd prefer a traffic-splitting approach. Do you have an API for changing weights programmatically?

Also, if you can paste a tiny Node snippet inline showing the recommended retry/backoff pattern that would be helpful for our engineers to skim before the call.

—Chris
